scope: Qualified OMP 18.0.9 macOS arm64, Windows x64, and Linux x64 clients; the digest-pinned RTX 5090 runtime image a62dd5b8 (runtime v0.6.2, source 63f28c95, binary 6ab904d7) under deployment profile qwen38-5090-v0.6.2 (configuration 5eb8a557); the RTX 4090 native package v0.6.1-beta.1 (runtime fork 63f28c95, the mainline runtime built for Ada, with the managed graceful stop); the RTX 3090 durable v0.2.5-beta.1 package (131,072-token context). All three lanes now serve from one runtime tree: the RTX 5090 container lane moved off its feat/warm-arrival branch head onto the mainline commit both native lanes build from, and was qualified on the owner appliance on 2026-09-10 (7/7 gates, EXP-030) and re-verified on 2026-09-11 against the published image pulled anonymously by digest. The RTX 4090 and RTX 3090 components, their profiles, and the OMP client are byte-identical to v0.6.1 and carry their receipts by hash. The RTX 3090 mainline candidate still ships separately when its host returns.

rtx5090.lifecycle: candidate and published-image runs both started and stopped through tools/lifecycle/ninfer_container.py (preflight bound image id, binary, model artifact, and configuration identity); the configuration identity computed from the published image equals the qualified one, so the profile did not drift between qualification and publication

rtx5090.post_restart_branch_reuse: private_long_anchor (8/8 across both sizes; no root re-prefill)
rtx5090.warm_arrival: both orders hot after a verified restart: resume-first 4.386 s resume then forks at 2.876 s and 1.353 s, fork-first likewise hot; every resume quoted the planted keys exactly
rtx5090.agent_protocol: fork/delete/no-resurrection across docker restart passed on the published image and on the candidate
rtx5090.origin_authentication: inherited from v0.4.7 (store format unchanged; the lifecycle candidate loaded MAC-tagged generations from a fresh store)
rtx5090.measured_on: published image a62dd5b8 for retrieval, decode, agent protocol, identity, auth boundary and completion; the appliance-built image of the same bytes for fanout, warm arrival and restore

rtx4090_windows_native.protocol_checks: 15/15 at the shipped pool and 15/15 at 8 host state slots
rtx4090_windows_native.rollback: bidirectional; candidate stopped by signal, predecessor by what its record declares

rtx3090_windows_native.carried_from: v0.5.0 (component byte-identical; requalified on its own rig on 2026-09-05 with origin-authenticated checkpoints)

interpretation: All three GPU lanes are qualified in one public release, and from this release they are built from one runtime tree; every claim binds an exact package, profile, and receipt.

The RTX 5090 container lane moved from its feat/warm-arrival branch head to the mainline runtime at 63f28c95 on the unchanged v0.4.8 argument set. Throughput is within run-to-run noise of v0.5.1 (prefill 2,169.9 vs 2,180.3 tok/s; decode 132.53 vs 133.13 tok/s) and every durability gate holds: a 5.2 GB session restores in 3.6-4.0 s with exact retrieval, a flipped payload byte is refused, and 8/8 sibling forks stay on the shared anchor across a verified restart.

Publication evidence is measured on the published bytes: every release asset was downloaded anonymously and hashed on a workstation, the image was pulled anonymously by digest with an empty credential store, and the lane's own gate script then ran against that pulled image.

The RTX 4090 and RTX 3090 components carry unchanged from v0.6.1 by hash; the RTX 4090's managed graceful stop and the RTX 3090's package are exactly the bytes that release qualified. The RTX 3090 mainline candidate ships separately when its host returns.
Raw prompts, model outputs, private host identifiers, and raw request logs are excluded.
